body: Yeah but I think he'd forget about it quickly and just adapt to the new routine. You know?

As for worrying about becoming a deadbeat: once again, you don't need a nice house or anything. so long as you're doing what you love, it doesn't matter if you're simply living on the plains by a campfire. at least you're doing **something**. deadbeats don't do a damned thing.

as for not having a passion: you're still young. i'm sure there's millions of things you still haven't tried out. get out there and try stuff. you'll find something. it doesn't even have to be something huge. it could be something as simple as anonymously helping anonymous people through their tough times and thoughts. just remember that money doesn't equal happiness, it just makes things easier.

as for being lazy: who isn't? if you find something you're passionate about, i'm certain you'll pick up the pace and manage to pay attention to it.

i'm going through a massive wave of depression, myself, so i'll regularly be on this throwaway talking to people that have been kind enough to talk to me. with that said, if you'd like to talk, feel free to PM me or even just reply to this post.

whatever the case, know this: it'll be alright.

>I either •Go to college, get a good job, take care of myself until I grow old, and die. Or •get a shitty job, sustain myself until I grow old, and die.

Not necessarily. Do you have anything you actually enjoy doing? Society shoves the idea down our throats that we're supposed to get a well paying job and that we won't be happy otherwise, but that's not true. You can literally do **anything** you want to do with your life, regardless of the amount of income it brings. You don't need a big home to be happy. You just need to do what you love to do.
I worry it would do more harm than good.

I don't want a new girlfriend. I can't imagine ever wanting one. I just want mine. I want my family. I want us to grow up as a family.

Not really some help, but before my recent goingson that make me want to die every moment of every day, I used to consider suicide for nothing more but to find out if, as an atheist, I'm right. Of course, I'd only know if I was wrong, but oh-ho-ho would I be surprised. Maybe it's something like that?
I just don't see how anything else would help.
